headline: Morgan Stanley Warns Brazil Stocks Could Fall 30% on Fiscal Worries
summary: Morgan Stanley stated that Brazilian stocks could drop 20% to 30% and the dollar could reach 5.70 reais if fiscal concerns escalate following Lula's election win.
why: Global investment bank forecasts influence institutional capital flows and foreign exchange sentiment toward emerging markets. Brazil's fiscal policy trajectory is a primary driver for local asset valuations.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Growing fiscal anxiety tends to drive capital outflows, weakening the local currency against the US dollar.

impacts.name: Brazilian Equities
impacts.why: Downward earnings revisions and higher risk premiums depress equity valuations during fiscal stress.

why_moved: High-profile institutional warnings regarding fiscal deficits and currency devaluation trigger risk-off repositioning among international investors in Brazilian assets.
